You can use sentences with if to talk hypothetically about the past.
You use the Past Perfect form of the if-clause and a past modal in the main clause.

If + Past Perfect + Past modal
would have, could have, might have

Note: People often say If I would have instead of If I had, but this is not correct in writing.
You should have told her about that important matter.
If I had spent more time with him, I might have seen that he was sleeping more than usual.
If I had known that, I would have asked you to pick me up one, and a brownie too.

You use a reporting verb like to say or to tell about what someone said in a conversation.

For example: She said (that) my cat needed some additional tests.

Reported questions are one form of reported speech.
You usually introduce reported questions with the verb to ask.

Here are some examples:
The vet asked (me) if/whether... (YES/NO questions)
The nurse asked (me) why/when/where/what/how... (question-word questions)

You may need to change pronouns and tense as well as time and place in reported questions.
The word order is like that of a normal statement (subject-verb-object).

Example: They told me they needed to draw some blood.

images.text:
Sally: Hey, where are you?
Vanessa: I'm just leaving Starbucks, grabbed a cappuccino.
Sally: If I had known that, I would have asked you to pick me up one, and a brownie too.
Vanessa: Need a chocolate fix?
Sally: Yeah ... I just got some upsetting news from the vet. I'm a bit of a mess.
Vanessa: What? Is Meenee sick? You didn't tell me that.
Sally: Well, I took him in for his yearly checkup. They told me they needed to draw some blood after a physical examination.

Vanessa: And?
Sally: They said that there are some grave concerns about his heart. They don't expect him to live through the winter.
Vanessa: I'm so sorry to hear that. Did the vet suggest anything to improve his quality of life?
Sally: The nurse said that there was very little I could do apart from keeping him comfortable.
Vanessa: That would have been devastating to hear.
Sally: I just feel so guilty. I should have recognized that there was a problem.

Vanessa: Don't be ridiculous! You are a devoted pet owner. Meenee's your fur baby!
Sally: I know but there were signs, now that I think of it. If I had spent more time with him, I might have seen that he was sleeping more than usual.
Vanessa: Don't beat yourself up about it. You couldn't have been any more committed to him. He is now on medication, right?
Sally: I just feel so lost. He's like a family member, you know?
Vanessa: I understand. I'm turning around in the parking lot. Your cappuccino and brownie are on their way!

Dealing with a sick or injured pet can be difficult. Imagine you have just received a phone call from the veterinarian to say that your pet is seriously ill. What is their diagnosis?
Instructions:
Write a 150-170 word diary entry about the phone call and your reaction to the news.
Include the date and greeting Dear Diary,
Describe your pet. Is it a dog? Bird? Horse?
Write about why you took your pet to a veterinary clinic. What symptoms did it have?
What does the staff say? What is their diagnosis? Quote the veterinarian in a written way.
Example: She said that they could give him some medication for the pain.
 What was your reaction to the news? Were you devastated?
Write three sentences about hypothetical situations in the past.
Examples:
  • If I had spent more time with him, I might have seen that he was sleeping more than usual.
  • If I had known that, I would have asked you to pick me up one, and a brownie too.
    •  Did you call anyone?
    Example: I immediately called my best friend.
     What are the next steps? What do you plan to do in the future?
    When you have typed in ALL your answers, click the Go to Writing Task button.

    My Diary Entry
It's time to review your diary entry about your pet.

When you are writing your diary entry, remember to:
  • Describe your pet.
  • Describe your reaction to the news.
  • Quote the veterinarian in a written way.
Proofread your diary entry for any spelling, grammar or punctuation errors.
Read your diary entry aloud to a partner.
Click the Submit button to save your work.
